skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Guides agents through creating isolated Git worktrees, selecting storage locations, verifying ignores, running setup, and checking baseline tests.
skill.summary: Guides AI coding agents through safe Git worktree setup and baseline verification.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting or documented Git workflow commands, not executable Ruby backticks or hidden secret access. Real risks remain where the skill asks the agent to run package managers, test commands, use repository-provided preferences, and commit ignore changes without explicit approval. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running package installation, build, or test commands in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Repository file can influence worktree location
remediation.suggestion: Validate CLAUDE.md worktree preferences against an allowlist and ask before using any unusual path.
Edit .gitignore only after approval and ask before creating any commit.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Dependency and Test Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to run package installation, build, and test commands automatically. These commands can execute project-controlled scripts and download dependencies.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup and baseline sections explicitly list package manager, build, and test commands. Those tools commonly execute repository code, so the risk is concrete for untrusted projects.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Repository Preference Controls Worktree Location
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to read CLAUDE.md for a worktree directory and use the preference without asking. A repository-controlled file could steer filesystem writes unless allowed paths are enforced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to use a CLAUDE.md preference without asking is explicit, but the later case block implies some expected locations. The missing validation still creates a plausible unsafe write-location risk.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Repository Commit Instruction

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly says to add a .gitignore line and commit it. It is a workflow integrity risk rather than a malicious payload.

content.value_statement: Developers need isolated workspaces before agents change code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through repeatable Git worktree setup and baseline checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects between .worktrees, worktrees, and a global config location using ordered checks.
Checks CLAUDE.md for repository-specific worktree directory preferences.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are ignored before creation.
Creates a new worktree and branch with Git worktree commands.
Detects common project files and runs matching setup commands.
Runs baseline tests and reports failures before implementation continues.
limitations: Requires an existing Git repository with worktree support.
Package setup commands can run project scripts and should be approved for untrusted code.
Does not choose branch names or feature scope by itself.
Does not replace repository-specific onboarding documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Development
use_cases.description: Create an isolated branch workspace before implementing a feature with an AI assistant.

use_cases.title: Handle Urgent Fixes
use_cases.description: Open a clean hotfix workspace without disturbing current local changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Setup
use_cases.description: Give AI coding agents a repeatable process for worktree location, setup, and baseline testing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated Git worktree for my next feature. Ask before installing dependencies or changing git history.

prompt_templates.title: Follow Repository Preferences
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect existing worktree directories and repository guidance. Validate the location with me before creating the worktree.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Tested Feature Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a worktree for feature <name>, run approved setup commands, run baseline tests, and report any failures before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Branch Worktree Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For two planned branches, propose safe worktree locations, required setup commands, test checks, and cleanup notes before creating anything.

output_examples.input: I need to build a login feature without disturbing my current branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the selected worktree location, confirms ignore protection, creates the feature workspace, and states whether baseline tests passed.

output_examples.input: Prepare a worktree for a hotfix and verify the baseline.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a clean hotfix workspace, runs approved setup steps, summarizes test results, and asks before proceeding if tests fail.

output_examples.input: Our repository has custom worktree guidance. Use it safely.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks repository guidance, validates the requested location, asks about unusual paths, and then follows the approved setup process.

best_practices: Approve dependency installation and test execution before using the skill on untrusted repositories.
Keep worktree directories ignored when they are inside the project.
Record the final worktree path and baseline test result before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Creating a project-local worktree before checking ignore rules.
Running setup commands from an unknown repository without user approval.
Continuing implementation after baseline tests fail without reporting the failures.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI coding assistant create a separate Git worktree before starting implementation work.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. The workflow can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can run Git commands.

faq.question: Will it modify my repository?
faq.answer: It can create a worktree, create a branch, and suggest .gitignore changes. Review those actions before approval.

faq.question: Why does it check ignore rules?
faq.answer: Ignored worktree directories reduce the chance of accidentally tracking nested workspace files.

faq.question: Can it run dependency installation?
faq.answer: Yes, it recommends common setup commands. Confirm those commands first when the repository is not fully trusted.

faq.question: What happens if tests fail?
faq.answer: The skill tells the assistant to report failures and ask whether to investigate or continue.
